          UEFA Champions League Match Predictions: The Opta Supercomputer’s Picks for This Week
        
      
                          
                      Oct 19, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the AI-powered Opta supercomputer, we provide our UEFA Champions League match predictions for every game across the 2026-27 competition.

The Opta supercomputer will again be with us every step of the way in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League as the model works to provide you with data-backed predictions for all matches and season outcomes.

Paris Saint-Germain have won back-to-back Champions League crowns after their penalty-shootout win over Arsenal in last season’s final, and they are among the favourites once again this time around. Real Madrid were the last team to win the UCL in three consecutive seasons, doing so in 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2017-18.

The Spanish giants, alongside rivals Barcelona, will be among the leading contenders in 2026-27, along with a host of Premier League clubs. There will be five English top-flight teams competing in the league phase this time around, with Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool among the favourites, and Manchester United alongside Aston Villa in the chasing pack.

Bayern Munich haven’t won the Champions League since 2020, but will undoubtedly be in the mix again this season, while Serie A clubs Inter Milan, Como, Napoli and Roma will be hoping to end a 17-year wait for an Italian winner.
Below, Opta Analyst provides detailed predictions for each game from Matchday 2, powered by thousands of simulations from the Opta supercomputer.
After a record-breaking matchday last week, the UEFA Champions League returns for gameweek three of the league phase.
There were more goals scored on MD2 (78) than on any previous matchday in UCL history, and fans will hope to see many more as the action kicks off with two early games in Turkey and Azerbaijan.

Sabah earned their first-ever win in the UEFA Champions League (outside of qualifiers) last week, beating Slavia Prague 2-0 thanks to two second-half goals. They face a much harder test in front of their own fans this week, though, coming up against Bundesliga side Borussia Dortmund.

Borussia Dortmund have won all four of their matches against Azerbaijani opponents in European competition (including qualifiers), and the Opta supercomputer is backing them to make it five from five this week. BVB won 68.9% of its 10,000 pre-game simulations.

After that defeat to Sabah on MD2, Slavia Prague head to Fenerbahçe looking to win their first points of the UCL campaign. The Opta supercomputer isn’t too confident on their chances of doing that, though, with the Turkish side winning 55.1% of its pre-game simulations.

Fenerbahçe were comprehensively thrashed 6-0 at Aston Villa last week, but they might be facing the perfect opponent to bounce back. Slavia have now gone 21 consecutive Champions League matches without a win (D7 L14).

The standout match on Tuesday night is Paris Saint-Germain vs Barcelona, with two of the biggest clubs in world football currently occupying first and second place in the league-phase table after two matchdays.

Reigning champions PSG will be looking for a third successive win against Barcelona. Only Bayern Munich (May 2015-October 2022) has ever done that previously in UCL history. The Opta supercomputer had a hard time picking a winner in this tie, but PSG just edged it (39.7%) over Barcelona (37.7%) in the pre-match sims.

Most eyes on Tuesday will be on this game, and for good reason. Of fixtures played 10+ times in European Cup/Champions League history, only Ajax vs Bayern Munich (3.9) has a higher goals-per-game ratio than Paris Saint-Germain vs Barcelona (3.8 – 57 goals in 15 meetings).
Manchester City lost 4-2 in an action-packed meeting with PSG last week and will look to return to form with a home game against AEK Athens.

The last team from outside of Europe’s big five leagues to win away at Man City in the Champions League was Basel in March 2018 (1-2). Since then, they are unbeaten in 15 (W12 D3), averaging three goals per match (3.1 – 46 in total).

AEK will also come up against the red-hot Erling Haaland, who now has 61 goals in 60 UEFA Champions League appearances, including 27 in 22 matches against teams from outside the top five European leagues.
The threat of Haaland is one reason for the Opta supercomputer’s lopsided match prediction, with City winning 83.0% of its simulations and the Greek club winning just 6.8%.
Liverpool are another side heavily backed to win at home on MD3, with the Premier League side defeating Villarreal across 61.4% of 10,000 pre-match simulations.
